open_questions: Duration remains long even with Gaia radius 0.414-0.424 (ratio 1.29-1.32) and fit_log_density_ratio -1.859 suggests residual offset/blemish; Gaia/ground-based radius for M dwarf should be confirmed

Coincidence signal period 0.635218 d equals rotation_d 0.635 exactly (signal_over_rotation 1.0003433070866141, false_alarm ~10^-89, amplitude 32989 ppm and 29239 ppm) with phase_curve amplitude 15960 ppm ratio_to_depth 1.213 chi2 544 dof 9 highly significant; light curve is dominated by spot modulation at same period - any spot-induced shape is ruled out by flat bottom but still requires check that modulation does not bias depth/density

Star is cool M-dwarf Teff 3250 K mass 0.3254 Msun, rapid rotator; spot cross-talk should be tested with radial velocities or higher-resolution transit photometry to confirm achromatic transit and flat bottom not spot artifact
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 1.25-hour, 4.3 Earth-radius dip every 0.635 days on the M dwarf itself, with no neighbour capable of faking it and no odd-even or secondary eclipse. The depth is shallow and flat-bottomed, consistent with a planet rather than a binary. The signal period exactly matches the star's rapid 0.635-day rotation, but the strong spot signal and long duration are best explained by an M-dwarf radius larger than the catalog value and by spots, not by an eclipsing binary.
